sentences.text: BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE ROOPESH CHANDRA VARSHNEY  ON THE 3 rd OF OCTOBER, 2024
MISC. APPEAL No. 1414 of 2023  THE NEW INDIA ASSURANCE
Versus  USHA DEVI AND OTHERS  Appearance:
Shri B.K.Agrawal, learned counsel for the appellant.

Shri Vibhore Kumar Sahu, learned counsel for respondents No. 1 to 3.
 Shri Ajay Raghuvanshi, learned counsel for respondents No. 4 and 5.

ORDER Appellant/Insurance Company has filed this appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 assailing the impugned award dated 6/12/2022 passed by Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ashoknagar in MACC No. 26/2022; whereby, respondents no. 1 to 3 claimants have been awarded a compensation of Rs. 28,53,000/- for the death of one Ranjeet, husband of respondent No. 1 and father of respondents No. 2 and 3, in road accident dated 25/5/2022.

2. Briefly stated facts of the case are that on 25/5/2022 when deceased Ranjeet was going on motorcycle over Railway Over Bridge Ashoknagar for doing Porter's job, it is alleged the truck No.
UP92T9154 coming from opposite side being driven by its driver in a very rash and negligent manner dashed the motorcycle of deceased, due to which he suffered grievous injuries and succumbed to the same.

Therefore, respondents No. 1 to 3 NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:17496 2 MA-1414-2023 claimants filed a claim case under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 seeking total compensation of Rs. 1,90,50,000/-; however, by the impugned award, learned Claims Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs. 28,53,000/- alongwith interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim case and liability for payment of compensation amount has been fixed over appellant and respondents No. 4 and 5 jointly and severally.

sentences.text: Learned Claims Tribunal while assessing the monthly income of deceased Rs. 15,000/- awarding 40% towards future prospects deducting 1/3 towards personal expenses, awarding Rs. 16,500/- each under the head loss of estate and funeral expenses and Rs. 1,32,000/- towards loss of consortium

,
calculated the impugned award amount.
4. It is the submission of learned counsel for the Insurance Company that learned Claims Tribunal erred in assessing the income of deceased at Rs. 15,000/- per month which is on higher side.
Deceased was engaged in the work of Hammal (Porter) and it is impossible that an man engaged in such job earning Rs. 15,000/- per month by getting work for whole month i.e. 30 days.

It is further submitted that learned Claims Tribunal also erred in awarding Rs. 44,000/- towards loss of consortium to each claimants whereas in light of catena of decisions of Apex Court, Rs. 40,000/- at the most can be awarded under the head loss of consortium.
5. Learned counsel for the respondents No. 1 to 3 opposed the prayer and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

6. Learned counsel for respondents No. 4 and 5 submitted that on the date of accident, offending truck was duly insured with the appellant NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:17496 3 MA-1414-2023 Insurance Company and liability has been primarily fastened over the Insurance Company as such it is internal matter between appellant and respondents no. 1 to 3.
7.
Heard learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the record.

8. From perusal of record, it is evidence that learned Claims Tribunal assessed the income of deceased at Rs. 15,000/- on the basis of evidence produced on behalf of claimants of another Hamaal, as such in the opinion of this Court such cannot be a criteria to assess the income and income is required to be assessed on proper appreciation of evidence available documentary as well as oral.
Accordingly, in the opinion of this Court, the income of deceased as assessed by the Claims Tribunal is on the higher side and same is assessed at Rs. 9,000/- per month.

As regards amount awarded under the head loss of consortium, in the opinion of this Court, learned Claims Tribunal erred in awarding amount under the head loss of consortium to each of the claimants, whereas, an amount of Rs. 44,000/- to wife of deceased is required to be awarded in light of most celebrated decision of Apex Court in the matter of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors., (2017)16SCC680.
9.

sentences.text: Accordingly while assessing the income of deceased at Rs. 9,000/- per month, his annual income comes to Rs. 1,08,000/- to which 1/3 is required to be deducted under the head personal expenses and after deducting the same, remaining amount comes to Rs. 72,000/-.

Now 40% to the established incomes is required to be added under the future prospects and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:17496 4 MA-1414-2023 after adding the same, the amount comes to Rs.
28,800/- and after adding the same, years loss of dependency comes to Rs. 1,00,800/-.
Now the multiplier of 16 would be applicable as per impugned award and after applying the multiplier, total loss of dependency comes to Rs. 1,00,800 x 16 = 16,12,800/- .
Claimants shall also be entitled to receive a sum of Rs. 16,500/- each under the head funeral expenses and loss of estate and Rs.

sentences.text: As such, the total amount of compensation to which claimants are entitled for comes to Rs. 16,89,800/-.

The Claims Tribunal by the impugned award has awarded a total compensation of Rs. 28,53,000/- therefore, same is liable to be deducted by a sum of Rs.
11,63,200/-.
10.

In view of the aforesaid discussion, the appeal filed by Insurance Company is allowed in part and claimants are held entitled to receive total compensation of Rs. 16,89,800/- as such impugned award is directed to be deducted by a sum of Rs. 11,63,200/-.
The amount of compensation shall carry interest as per impugned award.
Rest of the conditions as imposed by Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.
11. Impugned award is modified to the extent indicated hereinabove.

(ROOPESH CHANDRA VARSHNEY) JUDGE JPS/-
